reason: The cited lines show the tool passes an agent/request-supplied value to fillFormElement on the browser page, which can deliver data into a web page, so SINK is supported. They also show the tool can include a page snapshot in the response; page snapshots can contain non-public page data and attacker-controlled page content, so SECRET and UNTRUSTED are supported. Nothing in the cited lines shows arbitrary code execution on the host; browser/page interaction is not HOSTEXEC.
